title: MaxCut approximation with QAOA

problem.name: Maximum cut
problem.statement_latex:
Given nonnegative weights $w_{uv}$, maximize $C(z)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}w_{uv}(1-z_uz_v)/2$ over $z\in\{-1,1\}^n$, or return a cut meeting a specified approximation ratio. Sparse regular graphs are a central QAOA benchmark.
Complexity uses quantum gate and sample counts, classical arithmetic time for approximation, and classical bit complexity for exact finite-precision instances.
problem.statement_text: Given nonnegative weights $w_{uv}$, maximize $C(z)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}w_{uv}(1-z_uz_v)/2$ over $z\in\{-1,1\}^n$, or return a cut meeting a specified approximation ratio. Complexity uses quantum gate and sample counts, classical arithmetic time for approximation, and classical bit complexity for exact finite-precision instances.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(p(m+n))$ gates per sample, depth-$p$ QAOA; $O(KSp(m+n))$ for $K$ objective evaluations with $S$ shots each.
quantum.details_latex: The cost includes the problem-phase and mixer layers; synthesis precision contributes additional factors. On 3-regular graphs, the $p=1$ analysis guarantees an approximation ratio of at least $0.6924$. Results on higher-girth graphs and larger depth have their own graph and parameter assumptions. The complete variational optimization includes the evaluations and samples represented by $K$ and $S$.

classical.headline_latex: Polynomial time with ratio $0.87856$, Goemans--Williamson; $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ for exact sparse unweighted MaxCut.
classical.details_latex: The approximation guarantee applies to general nonnegative weights. For unweighted graphs with $m=O(n)$, threshold counting and self-reduction give the exact subexponential bound. For arbitrary unweighted graphs and fixed $\varepsilon>0$, sampling $O_\varepsilon(n)$ edges and optimizing the sample gives value at least $\operatorname{OPT}-\varepsilon m$ with the same exponent. For constant $p$, bounded degree and a fixed finite algebraic gate set, the complete QAOA output distribution can be sampled classically in expected $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time; compiled gate count controls the corresponding statement for synthesized rotations.

strength.description_latex: The general QAOA runtime and approximation theorems establish no asymptotic advantage over the applicable classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: Approximation guarantees are rigorous for specified graph classes and depths. Empirical comparisons are tied to their tested instances and classical solvers.

hardware.description_latex: Small superconducting-processor demonstrations exist. A circuit uses $n$ data qubits plus ancillas; useful large-depth operation needs accurate two-qubit gates, repeated sampling and parameter optimization. Fault-tolerant estimates also include rotation synthesis.
